claims.text: At stage-4 Đơn Hàng has one team of seven: a product owner, a scrum master, four developers and a tester, as in sprint-example.md; it owns the whole system.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/team-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 10-11; docs/team/sprint-example.md @ stage-4 lines 3-4

claims.text: multi-shop-requirements.md expects three to four teams to work on the system at 1,000 shops, against one team for one shop.
A group of n people has n(n-1)/2 pairs: 7 → 21, 14 → 91, 10 → 45, 6 → 15, 18 → 153.

The 'Đội hôm nay' table lists api (Ordering and Catalog modules), Notifications, Payments, DonHang.App, staging's platform, OpenTofu's cluster and platform layers, CI and one on-call rotation for all of it.

Only the team lead can change OpenTofu's cluster and platform layers (count 1); the last column counts people who can change a part without asking anyone, an assumption of the team; a one-person part stops when that person is away.
Adding people does not make each person know less: each still reviews and takes on-call for almost everything the team owns, so each person's cognitive load stays the same or grows.
Load also falls without new people by owning fewer things or making them easier to use, as the golden path does for adding a service; the golden path's defaults already meet the platform's rules.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/team-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 35-37; docs/team/golden-path.md @ stage-4 lines 3-6

claims.text: Per ADR 0025 the plan adds small teams each owning whole parts that change together: Đặt hàng (Ordering, Payments, Notifications, app ordering), Cửa hàng (Catalog, opening shops), Platform (OpenTofu, shared tools).
Each team has 5 to 7 people (assumed), sized by what it must know to change and run its parts, not by number of services or lines of code.
Platform is formed before the second team for a business flow; today's team becomes Đặt hàng.
Team boundaries follow existing module and service boundaries; because team boundaries later shape system boundaries, the plan draws no new boundary across a module.
Conway's law: a system's structure tends to mirror the communication structure of the organisation that builds it; two teams sharing one module must agree on each change, and its boundary blurs.

Small teams that each own whole parts that change together mean most changes need talk only inside one team, and each person mainly keeps that team's parts in mind (hedged; requests across teams remain a cost).
claims.source_hint: docs/team/team-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 41-42; lesson s4, s6 row 2, s8 bullet 2, s9

claims.text: The OpenTofu code in deploy/tofu/ is not a service, yet must be known; the api is one service holding two modules — so a service count is a poor measure of what a team can own.

Trade-offs: adding people fits a small system and growth of a person or two; small teams fit when module and service lines exist; one team per service is a rough first cut at most; lowering load fits overload without growing work.

Choices not written in Đơn Hàng's files: offered three more developers for a team of seven, look at what it owns and move or simplify a whole part; keep Ordering whole in one team rather than split it.

Possible symptoms (hedged): a grown team's reviews and daily meeting take longer while work per sprint does not rise with headcount; a small change waiting for the one person who knows another corner; a team with 'only two services' worn out by shared tools.
